circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, designed by Hermann Tilke, is a 5. 281-kilometer track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi that has hosted the Formula One season finale since 2009. It represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street-based motorsport venue situated around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting racing championships. The track maintains FIA Grade 1 classification status.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The Spielberg circuit in Austria spans 4. 326 kilometers and has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two separate eras, first as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, then following restructuring and renaming as the A1-Ring between 1997 and 2003. The track underwent significant modifications including a reduction in length during the interval between these two hosting periods.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street venue in Azerbaijan's capital that hosts Formula One racing along the city's boulevard, measuring approximately 6 km in length and ranking among the calendar's longest tracks. The circuit first welcomed a grand prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. Beyond F1, the venue has accommodated various motorsport categories including GP2 racing, endurance competitions, and Australian V8 Supercars events, while maintaining FIA Grade 1 certification with configurable track layouts.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian motor-racing venue situated near the town of Spa in the Walloon region. It has been the home of the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1950, with the exception of 2003 and 2006, and has continuously hosted the race annually since 1985.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre temporary street circuit that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond hosting Formula One, the track has been utilized by various international motorsports competitions, including sports car championships and North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in China's Jiading District served as the primary venue for the Chinese Grand Prix, hosting the event from 2004 to 2019 before resuming from 2024. The track has expanded its motorsport calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024, establishing itself as a key location for international racing competitions.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located in England near Northamptonshire, Silverstone Circuit has been the primary venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably staged the inaugural Formula One World Championship race in 1950. Following decades of shared hosting duties with Aintree and Brands Hatch, the circuit became the permanent home of Britain's grand prix from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the sport's first Grand Prix behind the Iron Curtain when it debuted in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue, the track was constructed outside the city near a highway after plans for a Monaco-style street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by the government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit located near Milan in northern Italy that opened in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. It annually hosts the Italian Grand Prix, with this prestigious event held there continuously since 1949 except for a 1980 closure during renovations.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, featuring a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track is primarily recognized as a prominent venue for both Formula One and Super Formula racing competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that winds through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding thoroughfares. The track passes iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues, including the Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of motorsport's most visually distinctive urban layouts.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez commemorates two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate incidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue returned to the Formula One calendar in 2015 after a 23-year absence, hosting what is now called the Mexico City Grand Prix on a revised track configuration distinct from its previous iterations used until 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 turns and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed specifically for Formula One racing by specialist circuit designers, the venue began hosting the Miami Grand Prix as a calendar addition in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine in the Principality of Monaco, spanning 3. 337 kilometers around the harbor area. Though officially named after the circuit itself, the track is typically known as Monte Carlo due to its location primarily within that neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: The 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit lies in the Dutch coastal dunes, approximately 35 km from Amsterdam, and hosts the Dutch Grand Prix following its return to the Formula One calendar in 2021. The venue will cease hosting Formula One after the 2026 season concludes.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419-kilometre racing venue situated near Lusail, north of Doha in Qatar, featuring a 1. 068-kilometre main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 status.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The venue hosts major international motorsport events and features additional karting facilities named after fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street venue in Saudi Arabia that has held the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually from 2021 onward, situated along the Red Sea waterfront. The track also began hosting a Formula E event in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based track that winds around the Marina Bay waterfront in Singapore, incorporating sections through the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of racing capabilities. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility in Austin, Texas that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside hosting major motorcycle and endurance racing events. The venue has also accommodated various other international motorsports series over the years, including rally and sports car championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand in the championship.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships in 2005 and 2006 with Renault and claimed 32 race victories over his 23-season career. Beyond his single-seater success, Alonso has achieved remarkable accomplishments in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24-hour victories and the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One's and the World Endurance Championship's premier titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured six race victories since entering the championship in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: British driver Oliver Bearman races for the Haas team in Formula One. He has been in a relationship with fellow racing driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli since 2022.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabriel Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team. He brings his motorsport background to the championship as one of the grid's competitors.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas has claimed ten race victories during his thirteen-year Formula One career and finished as championship runner-up twice while racing for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. He currently competes for Cadillac in the sport's top series.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One with Alpine. He represents his country in the sport's top motorseries.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve driver position with Haas while competing in European endurance racing with Nielsen Racing in the LMP2 category. He has participated in seven Formula One races during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri stands as a notable achievement in his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian racing driver who currently drives for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, racing under the French national designation.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple records in the sport, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in Formula One history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One after establishing himself as a competitive midfield competitor throughout his career. Beyond single-seater racing, he achieved significant success in sports car racing, notably securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor who currently drives for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured second place in the 2022 drivers' championship. Across his nine seasons in the sport, Leclerc has claimed nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW's factory team at WRT, while also taking part in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing. He previously raced in Formula One across two separate stints, from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British Formula One driver, secured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren. Over his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 12 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The accomplished competitor previously claimed victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 15 seasons. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while competing for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing in Formula One for McLaren, has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four-year tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", competed in Formula One throughout a 14-season career spanning 2011 to 2024, achieving eight race victories during his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell has secured seven Grand Prix victories during his eight-year Formula One career with Mercedes, where he currently races.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 class for Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda participated in Formula One competitions spanning from 2021 through 2025, currently holding a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competing for Red Bull Racing has secured four consecutive world championships spanning 2021 to 2024, establishing himself as one of Formula One's most dominant competitors with 71 Grand Prix victories across his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He currently supports the team in a development capacity while holding the distinction of being the only driver from his nation to have competed at the sport's highest level.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has raced as Alpine since 2021, continuing Renault's Formula One involvement following its rebranding from Renault F1 Team to promote the French manufacturer's sports car division. Alpine's only victory came through Esteban Ocon at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, with the team operating as Renault's works outfit until the manufacturer's withdrawal at the end of 2025 and currently competing with Mercedes power units.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One through different incarnations as a British manufacturer, with the present iteration operating under AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian automaker Ferrari, stands as the most storied and victorious team in Formula One history, participating continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" for their iconic emblem, they represent both the sport's longest-running competitor and its most decorated outfit.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with operations beginning in the 2016 season. Ayao Komatsu took over as team principal in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had led the outfit since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing outfit established in 1970, the team initially built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery as an independent constructor, winning two endurance championships including the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours. After competing in Formula One from 1993 onwards through numerous transformations, the team ceased operations in 2025 as the sport's fourth-longest-running constructor, having been acquired by Audi in 2024 to serve as the foundation for Audi's works team entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, which is owned by Bahrain's Mumtalakat Holding Company. The team competes under sponsorship arrangements in the sport's premier championship series.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with its current team based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The Mercedes-AMG Petronas team became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff from January 2022, sharing equal stakes. The team carries the historic "Silver Arrows" nickname associated with Mercedes' racing heritage.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two squads under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents the conglomerate's second constructor initiative in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of Red Bull's two teams. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the squad operates as Red Bull's second constructor alongside the primary Red Bull Racing outfit.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team based in England, was established in 2005 and has been a dominant force in modern Formula One under longtime principal Christian Horner until his departure in 2025. The team is one of two Formula One operations owned by Red Bull GmbH, with Laurent Mekies taking over leadership responsibilities following Horner's exit.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor founded by Frank Williams and Patrick Head in 1977, has become one of the sport's established teams. Operating from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team, following Frank Williams's earlier unsuccessful racing venture.
